transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Hello, Doctor. Well, the main reason I'm here is that my sleep has become completely unmoored lately. 

At first, I was waking up after maybe two or three hours, and I'd be up drafting plans—just feeling completely energized and ready to go. But now, it's changed. Now I just lie awake long before dawn, and my stomach is tight. I don't get any sense of rest at all anymore, and I just needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you had any periods recently where you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or irritable — maybe even needing less sleep but still feeling rested?

Yes, that's exactly what was happening when I was waking up early. For a few weeks, I felt... well, almost brilliantly optimistic. It seemed like every obstacle in my way was just trivial. 

But at the same time, if anyone questioned me or my plans, I got incredibly irritable. I snapped at them. It honestly felt like they were trying to sabotage me, like I was the only sensible man in the room and they were just getting in the way.
Have you experienced a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really felt sad or hopeless. I mean, lately I just feel awful because of the lack of sleep and that tightness in my stomach I mentioned, but it's not depression. It's just sheer exhaustion from lying awake. So, no, I haven't had a couple of weeks where I felt down like that.

Have you ever had a period of time when your mood was extremely elevated or irritable, and you were doing things that were unusual for you—like spending a lot of money, taking on too many projects, or acting recklessly?

Yes, I did take on quite a lot of projects. I mean... I'm retired now, so my schedule is usually pretty quiet. But during that time, I just felt this push to get things done. 

I started mentoring multiple companies all at once. I was up drafting these big fundraising campaigns, and... well, I was arranging lunches with half the town to get people on board with my ideas. Looking back on it, it was far beyond anything I would normally take on in retirement.

Has the period of feeling awful, lying awake, and experiencing tightness in your stomach lasted for at least two weeks, and has it felt like you’re no longer in that high-energy, optimistic state at all?

Well, the lying awake and that tight feeling in my stomach... yes, that's been going on for at least two weeks now. And no, I'm definitely not in that high-energy state anymore. I don't feel optimistic at all. I just feel drained and worn out from not sleeping.

During this time when you’ve felt drained and worn out, have you also experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in things you usually enjoy, or felt down and depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I have. I just don't have the interest in things anymore. I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or I'd just lose myself in photography and cooking. But lately... I look at my camera, or I think about going to the bridge table, and I feel absolutely nothing. Well, nothing except just thinking about the effort it would take to pretend I'm enjoying it. So, yes, I've definitely lost interest in the things I usually like to do.
Have you ever experienced a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, before this most recent change in your mood?

Well, this current stretch... it's actually been going on for a while. It's not just the last couple of weeks. This low feeling, just wanting to withdraw from everything and feeling guilty about it all... that's been happening for about nine months now, ever since all those big plans I was making just completely fell apart.

During that time when you felt so optimistic and full of energy, did you ever experience a period that lasted at least four consecutive days where you felt this way, with a clear change in your usual behavior and functioning?

I'm not really sure about the exact number of days, to be honest. I mean... it definitely lasted a while. Long enough for me to draw up all those big plans and really get going on them. But I wasn't keeping track of whether it was exactly four consecutive days or not. I just know I had this stretch of time where I was full of energy and acting quite different from my usual self, and then... well, then it all crashed. So I can't say for certain about the four days.

During that high-energy period when you were taking on all those projects and feeling very optimistic, did you ever go a full week without needing much sleep, or was there any time when others felt you were out of control or needed to be hospitalized?

Well, I'm not sure about the exact sleep or being hospitalized... but I do know that period lasted for weeks. I felt, I don't know, almost brilliantly optimistic. It was like every obstacle in my way was just trivial. I had so much energy for all these plans. But... well, if anyone questioned me or tried to slow me down, I would just snap at them. I felt like they were trying to sabotage me, like I was the only sensible man in the room and everyone else was just in the way.
During that high-energy period, did you have at least a full week where you didn’t need much sleep and your behavior was clearly out of character for you?

Well, like I was saying, I can't really put a finger on exactly how long the sleep thing went on. I just know that whole period of being really energized and irritable lasted for weeks. I definitely wasn't acting like my usual self during that stretch, but... I don't know if there was one specific week where I didn't sleep much. I just know the whole phase went on for a good while before everything fell apart.
During that high-energy period, was there at least one full week where you felt continuously energized and needed very little sleep, even if it was part of a longer stretch of time?

I... I really can't say for sure if there was one specific week where I continuously needed very little sleep. I mean, the whole period of feeling energized lasted for weeks, like I said, but I wasn't tracking my sleep well enough to say, "Yes, this one full week I barely slept." I just know I had a lot of energy overall during that time. I wish I could give you a more exact answer, but I just don't know.

Can you think back to when you were feeling very energetic and optimistic — was there at least one stretch of time, even within that longer period, where your mood was clearly different from your usual non-depressed mood and stayed that way for at least four days in a row?

To be honest, breaking it down into a specific number of days... it's just not something I can do. I know that entire phase lasted for weeks, and yes, my mood was definitely very different from how I normally am. But as for whether it stayed exactly like that for four days in a row without any break or shift... I really couldn't tell you. 

I wasn't keeping a journal or tracking my moods day by day. Looking back on it now, it all just blends together into one long stretch, so I really don't know if there was a specific four-day block like you're asking about.

Can you recall if there was a time when you felt extremely energetic, euphoric, or irritable for at least seven consecutive days without a break, where your mood was clearly different from your usual self?

I understand you're looking for a specific number of days, but... I just can't give you that. Like I mentioned, the whole thing lasted for weeks. I was definitely extremely energetic, and very irritable, and completely unlike my usual self for that entire period. 

But if you're asking whether there was a solid seven-day block without a single dip or break in there... I simply don't have that level of detail in my memory. I just know it was a long, intense phase, and I can't break it down into exact days for you.

During that time you felt so energetic and irritable, was there a period of at least seven days in a row where your mood was so high or unstable that it clearly affected how you functioned in your daily life, even if others didn't point it out to you?

I know we keep coming back to the exact number of days, but I still don't have a precise answer for you. Did it affect my daily life? Yes, absolutely. My whole routine was completely turned upside down for those weeks. 

But as for whether there was a strict seven-day period in a row where it consistently impacted my functioning... I just don't know. I wasn't paying attention to the calendar or measuring how well I was doing day by day. I was just too wound up. It's all just one long, disruptive blur to me now, so I really can't single out a specific week like that.
During that time you felt so energetic and irritable, was there a period when it lasted for at least seven days straight without a break, even if you weren't keeping track at the time?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles a bit with this. I know you're trying to pin down a specific timeline, but I really have to give you the exact same answer. I just don't know. 

The whole thing went on for weeks, but as for a continuous, uninterrupted seven days straight... I just can't say for sure. I don't mean to be difficult, it's just... it's impossible for me to look back and carve out a specific week like that. I simply don't have that kind of memory of it.

Looking back, can you say for certain that there was at least one full week when your mood stayed extremely high, energetic, or irritable without any break, even if you weren't tracking it at the time?

Doctor, I... I really don't know how else to say this. I understand you need to know if it was exactly seven days, but I just cannot give you a yes or a no. 

I know it was weeks of being completely wired and agitated. But a full week, seven days, without a single break? I just don't have that level of detail in my memory. I'm sorry, but I really can't say for certain.
Looking back, even if you can’t be exact, was there a time when you felt extremely energetic, euphoric, or irritable for an entire week without any break at all in that mood?

Doctor, I... I really don't have a different answer for you. We've gone over this a few times now, and I just can't give you a definitive yes or no about an entire week without a single break. 

I know the whole thing lasted for weeks. I was completely wired during that time. But as for seven days straight with absolutely no break in the mood... I just don't know. I simply can't be more exact than what I've already told you.
Looking back, even if you can’t be exact, was there a time when you felt extremely energetic, euphoric, or irritable for an entire week without any break at all in that mood?

Doctor, I'm really trying here, but... I don't know how many different ways I can say it. You're asking the same thing again. 

I know it was weeks of feeling like that—just completely wound up. But I cannot tell you if there was a solid seven-day stretch without a single dip. I just don't have that kind of timeline in my head from back then. I really can't give you a better answer than that.
